audit.whatIsWrong: Five chart rows disagreed with the already-audited mirror and with their own whys text: the page had Levels 1, 2 and 6 as Skill and Levels 4-5 and First item as Fiora, while whys[0] through whys[5] all say the stages are Sett's. The lane was also graded 'Hard matchup' at 7/10 with a red tone on a 54.27% win rate over 2036 games, while diff said FAV.
audit.why: The mirror set rows 0, 1, 3, 4 and 5 to Sett with row 2 Skill and row 6 Fiora, matching the packet chart and the prose on both pages.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Sett / Sett / Skill / Sett / Sett / Sett / Fiora as one atomic paired group with ratings matched; diffRating to 6/10, tone to the even/favoured gold, and the final rating line to 'Favoured matchup'.

audit.whatIsWrong: Riposte was the tracked ability on every panel with no cooldown attached, and Lunge and Grand Challenge had none either.
audit.why: Riposte is 24/22/20/18/16s — the longest cooldown in her kit and a genuinely huge window at rank 1. Lunge is 13s at rank 1 but falls to 6s at rank 5, Bladework 11s, Grand Challenge 110/90/70s.
audit.corrected: 24s written into the cooldown panel, both do's, the don'ts, report[5], spikes[0] and phases[2]; Lunge's 13s into phases[1]; Grand Challenge's 110s into phases[4] and spikes[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: Two claims were wrong. spikes[1] and mid said The Show Stopper 'suppresses' and that the suppress 'ignores her Riposte timing'. And the page treated Facebreaker as an unconditional stun, which is what makes the Riposte interaction dangerous rather than merely awkward.
audit.why: Riot's text for The Show Stopper is carry, slam, damage and a landing slow — no suppression and nothing that beats a parry. Facebreaker only stuns when enemies are on opposite sides of Sett; caught on the same side as your own wave it is a slow. Riposte stuns her attacker back only if it blocked an immobilizing effect, so whether your Facebreaker is a stun or a slow decides whether baiting Riposte wrong costs you the trade or the kill. Also absent: Duelist's Dance heals her on every Vital, and Lunge applies on-hit effects.
audit.corrected: Suppression removed from spikes[1] and mid; the both-sides positioning rule written into spikes[0] and phases[3]; the Riposte-returns-a-stun consequence into the cooldown panel, dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[0].d and report[5]; the Vital heal into dontsFull[1].d and the anti-heal buy.
sources: champ-data/_kits/fiora.json (W stun condition, P heal, Q onHit)

audit.whatIsWrong: The missing-interactions file proposes that The Show Stopper's grounding shuts off Lunge. I did not write it.
audit.why: The grounding is a derived flag; Riot's own description of The Show Stopper mentions only the carry, the slam, the damage and a landing slow. Against Fiora that claim would change when you hold a 120s ultimate, so it needs verifying before anyone states it.

edits.before: Hard matchup — difficulty 7/10, Fiora carry threat 8/10.
edits.after: Favoured matchup — difficulty 6/10, Fiora carry threat 8/10.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 7/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Riposte and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 6/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Riposte and how disciplined your pattern is.

edits.before: Double-punch passive makes you the strongest level-1 auto-trader in the lane. Punish Fiora on every CS, but respect her opening tool — chips now, all-ins later.
edits.after: Your double-punch passive out-trades a fragile Fiora at level 1. Punish every last-hit, but stand off her Vitals — she heals off every one she hits.

edits.before: Q gives move speed toward Fiora and two empowered punches. Take short Q trades and back off before she can answer with Riposte.
edits.after: Knuckle Down's move speed and two empowered punches beat her pre-item bar. Lunge is 13s at rank 1 — trade while it is spent.

edits.before: Facebreaker is online — the E-stun into double punch + W is your full pattern. Run it the moment Fiora burns Riposte.
edits.after: Facebreaker is online at 16s, but Riposte parries it. Bait the 24s W out with an auto first, then run the pattern.

edits.before: Q ranks make your punch trades heavier, but Fiora has her core tools too. Keep the grit bar honest: trade in, W-shield her return damage, out.
edits.after: You keep tempo: bait Riposte, then Facebreaker, double punch, Haymaker. Pull her toward your wave so she is caught between you and the minions.

edits.before: The Show Stopper online — you can start fights Fiora doesn't want. Suplex her into your wave or tower, never into her own minions.
edits.after: The Show Stopper starts fights a squishy Fiora doesn't want, and Haymaker's true centre ignores her armour. Grand Challenge is 110s.

edits.before: Stridebreaker fixes your only weakness — sticking to Fiora. Shove, recall on the spike, and force the next trade before she matches your item.
edits.after: Stridebreaker fixes sticking to her through Lunge. Shove, recall on the spike, and force the trade before Trinity and Bork come online.

edits.before: Sterak's makes your all-in nearly unburstable. Fights are decided by whether you cash a max-grit W — track Riposte and commit on the gap.
edits.after: Two items and her Vital procs, true damage and lifesteal chew Grit faster than you burst. Play the map; don't hand her an isolated duel.

edits.before: - Fiora Riposte: matchup-defining — Parries your E-stun + stuns. Bait it. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - Fiora Riposte: matchup-defining — 24s at rank 1, parries all damage, and stuns you back if it blocks CC.

edits.before: Parries your E-stun + stuns. Bait it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 24s at rank 1. If it blocks your stun, the return stab stuns you back.

edits.before: Fiora wastes Riposte — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Bait the 24s Riposte with an auto, then run the pattern.

edits.before: That is Fiora's favourite window — refuse it and half her win condition is gone.
edits.after: Facebreaker into Riposte hands her a free stun on you — always bait it first.

edits.before: Burning your answer for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Duelist's Dance heals her on every Vital she hits — keep moving off them.

edits.before: Track Fiora's Riposte: Parries your E-stun + stuns. Bait it. When it is down — E-stun + W her.
edits.after: Track Riposte: 24s at rank 1, parries all damage, stuns you back if it blocks your CC.

edits.before: Start Doran's Blade + Health Potion. Core: Stridebreaker  (stick to them through the W panel window), then Sterak's Gage; boots Plated Steelcaps. First back: Executioner's Calling (≈800g) — his healing out-paces your grit trades.
edits.after: Start Doran's Blade + Health Potion. Core: Stridebreaker (stick to her through the Haymaker window), then Sterak's Gage; boots Plated Steelcaps. First back: Executioner's Calling (≈800g) — Vitals and Grand Challenge heal her through your chip.

edits.before: Level 6 your R slam deletes a squishy Fiora through her ult.
edits.after: Level 6 your slam plus true damage deletes a squishy Fiora.

edits.before: You win early trades — Fiora is fragile pre-items, so E Facebreaker to lock her, Q Knuckle Down slow, and W Haymaker the stored damage before she can Q Lunge to a minion and reset spacing; her Riposte (W) parries one CC but not your whole combo.
edits.after: You win early trades -- Fiora is fragile pre-items, so bait the 24s Riposte, then Facebreaker to lock her, Knuckle Down slow, and Haymaker the stored damage before Lunge resets spacing. Pull her toward your wave so she is caught on both sides and actually gets stunned.

edits.before: Your R The Show Stopper suppress ignores her Riposte timing if you bait it first, and the true-damage slam plus Grit Haymaker deletes a squishy Fiora; she can't R Grand Challenge you to death through your burst.
edits.after: The Show Stopper carries her 400 units out of her own wave and a full-Grit Haymaker's true centre follows -- a squishy Fiora doesn't survive it. Grand Challenge is 110s and heals her, so bait it or bring Grievous.

edits.before: Through 3-6 you keep bullying: bait Riposte, then E-Q-W her stored damage, and at 6 your R suppress-slam plus true damage is a kill button a squishy Fiora can't survive even with Grand Challenge.
edits.after: Through 3-6 you keep bullying: bait the 24s Riposte, then Facebreaker, punch, Haymaker, and at 6 the slam plus a true-damage centre is a kill button a squishy Fiora can't survive.

notes: The sharpest correction here is that Facebreaker is not an unconditional stun — Riot's text downgrades it to a slow when every enemy it catches is on one side of Sett. That matters more against Fiora than against anyone else, because Riposte only stuns her attacker back if it parried an immobilizing effect. So whether you are standing between her and your own wave decides whether a mistimed Facebreaker costs you a trade or hands her a free stun. The page had also built its level-6 kill on a 'suppress' The Show Stopper does not have.
